content: I have been looking around for areas to contribute in as well. @Shreyas Srinivas algolean is your repo/effort right ? I just read the paper by Leonardo de Moura about CSlib and its ambitions. Sounds pretty cool but directionally what areas are they/CSlib seeking contributions in? @Chris Henson

Fawad said:

I have been looking around for areas to contribute in as well. Shreyas Srinivas algolean is your repo/effort right ?

It started that way, because I have a concrete vision for algorithms and complexity that I intend to realise. Now it is expanding with academic contributors joining in and we will soon have an academic host as well. I’ll be giving another invited talk in a month. The goal is to build an algorithms and complexity library that is useful for researchers hoping to formalise frontier results. It’ll stay in synch with CSLib in some respects allowing upstreaming of relevant content, while we retain the freedom to pursue our design. I’d draw an analogy to the additive combinatorics library : https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/113486-General-announcements/topic/AddCombi.2C.20maths.20sublibrary.20for.20additive.20combinatorics/near/592703921

I am only responding here because you asked this question, but it might be slightly off topic otherwise and if you have questions, I recommend starting a new topic.
@Shreyas Srinivas I appreciate the attention to staying on-topic. This thread is a bit meandering anyway, so let me move this to a thread that can be a place to discuss any upstreaming.
2 messages were moved here from #CSLib > areas seeking contributions by Chris Henson.
Maybe the question also needs to be moved otherwise the asker might not get notified of this thread.
@Fawad : You could try edit distance algorithms. Even the naive n^2 algorithm would be nice
I had another idea, we might want the fast fourier transform, discrete cosine transform etc on ReadOnlyVecs
